classification.difficultyReason: Rationalise two denominators in each expression and combine the resulting terms to demonstrate cancellation of the surds.

content.prompt: Show that each expression is rational by first rationalising the denominators.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{3}{2+\sqrt{2}}&=\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{3(2-\sqrt{2})}{4-2}\\\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{3}{2+\sqrt{2}}&=\frac{3\sqrt{2}+6-3\sqrt{2}}{2}\\\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{3}{2+\sqrt{2}}&=3\end{align*}$$

The result is an integer, so it is rational.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{1}{3+\sqrt{6}}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}&=\frac{3-\sqrt{6}}{9-6}+\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{6}\\\frac{1}{3+\sqrt{6}}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}&=\frac{3-\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{6}}{3}\\\frac{1}{3+\sqrt{6}}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}&=1\end{align*}$$

The result is an integer, so it is rational.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{4}{2+\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{3-2\sqrt{2}}&=\frac{4(2-\sqrt{2})}{4-2}+\frac{3+2\sqrt{2}}{9-8}\\\frac{4}{2+\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{3-2\sqrt{2}}&=4-2\sqrt{2}+3+2\sqrt{2}\\\frac{4}{2+\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{3-2\sqrt{2}}&=7\end{align*}$$

The result is an integer, so it is rational.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{8}{3-\sqrt{7}}-\frac{6}{2\sqrt{7}-5}&=\frac{8(3+\sqrt{7})}{9-7}-\frac{6(2\sqrt{7}+5)}{28-25}\\\frac{8}{3-\sqrt{7}}-\frac{6}{2\sqrt{7}-5}&=12+4\sqrt{7}-(4\sqrt{7}+10)\\\frac{8}{3-\sqrt{7}}-\frac{6}{2\sqrt{7}-5}&=2\end{align*}$$

The result is an integer, so it is rational.
